# Uniform energy shape envelopes and the finite-contact buffered credit

This note proves the uniform analytic input for actual buffered-cover
continuation. It allows signed radial speeds, so the energy expansion
does not require nested bodies. Its unnormalized nested application
then gives the safe contact-minimum improvement of the fixed-threshold
quantile construction. It does not presume a differentiable path of
deepest points or substitute one chosen source for all old contacts.

The original buffered region, fixed-face rigidity and notation are in
`candidate 86dd5366456916a8`.
The exact fixed-threshold continuation is Section 5 of
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. Actual signed radial hypotheses

Let K_t be convex bodies in R^d, d>=1, with K_0=K, for t>=0 small.
Fix o in int K. For an old boundary point X let its new radial endpoint
be

    o+(1-s_t(X))(X-o).

Assume that these endpoints describe K_t on every ray, and that for
one fixed C and a bounded measurable SIGNED function v,

    |s_t(X)|<=Ct,
    s_t(X)/t -> v(X)/H(X)  surface-almost everywhere,
    H(X)=n(X).(X-o)>0.                                  (1)

Here n is the unique outward normal at regular boundary points.
In dimension one use the two endpoints and H_0 measure. Convex-body
boundaries are regular surface-almost everywhere, and an inner ball
about o bounds H away from zero. These are explicit hypotheses about
the actual bodies, not a consequence of Hausdorff continuity alone.

The absolute radial bound implies two-sided homothetic containment,
Hausdorff convergence K_t->K, a common inner ball, and bounded volumes.
It also gives the first volume derivative

    |K_t|=|K|-t integral_(boundary K) v dS+o(t).          (2)

Negative v represents outward motion and is allowed throughout the
analytic statements below.

## 2. Uniform projective objective expansion

Let U be any compact subset of int K. For y in U write N=d+1 and

    E(y)=min_a I_0(a,y),
    I_t(a,y)=integral_(K_t)[1+a.(X-y)]^(-N)dX.

The minimizers a_t(y) are defined for small t because U remains inside
K_t. They lie in a common compact admissible parameter set for the
OLD bodies as well as the new ones. Indeed a fixed-radius ball about
each y bounds ||a_t(y)|| uniformly. Optimal projective denominators
are at least 1/N on their own bodies. Matching points of K and K_t
within O(t) therefore bounds their denominators below by 1/(2N) on K
for all small t, uniformly in y. The old minimizers obey the same
compact bounds. Slightly enlarging the physical neighborhood still
leaves a common positive denominator floor.

For every such compact parameter set the oriented radial shell formula
is

    I_0(a,y)-I_t(a,y)
      =integral_(boundary K) integral_0^(s_t(X))
          [1+a.(o+(1-r)(X-o)-y)]^(-N)
          H(X)(1-r)^(d-1) dr dS(X).                    (3)

When s_t is negative the inner integral has its usual negative
orientation and accounts exactly for added volume. All integrands
are uniformly bounded and uniformly Lipschitz in the physical point,
because of the common positive denominator floor. Replacing the
inner weight by its value at X and (1-r)^(d-1) by one costs O(t^2),
uniformly in (a,y). Assumption (1) and dominated convergence give

    H s_t/t -> v  in L1(dS).

The common uniform weight bound therefore gives the UNIFORM expansion

    I_t(a,y)=I_0(a,y)-t J(a,y)+o(t),
    J(a,y)=integral_(boundary K)[1+a.(X-y)]^(-N)v(X)dS.  (4)

The function J is continuous on the compact admissible parameter set,
even when v is merely bounded measurable.

## 3. Uniform minimization over the projective parameter

The old minimizing parameter a_0(y) is unique and continuous on U;
strict parameter convexity and the positive Hessian also give its
usual smooth local dependence on the interior mark. The new
minimizers converge uniformly to it:

    sup_(y in U)||a_t(y)-a_0(y)|| -> 0.                 (5)

To prove (5), any alleged contrary sequence has a subsequence with
y_t->y and a_t(y_t)->a. Uniform convergence of I_t to I_0 and
minimality identify a with the unique minimizer a_0(y). Continuity of
the old minimizer contradicts the alleged separation.

Evaluating (4) at the old minimizer supplies the upper expansion bound.
Evaluating at the new minimizer, using I_0(a_t,y)>=E(y), supplies the
lower bound. Equation (5) and uniform continuity of J identify their
first-order coefficients uniformly in y. Hence

    E_(K_t)(y)=E_K(y)-t C_E(y)+o(t), uniformly on U,
    C_E(y)=integral_(boundary K)
            [1+a_0(y).(X-y)]^(-d-1)v(X)dS.             (6)

The coefficient C_E is continuous in y. Since E is uniformly positive
on U, for every fixed r>0 the corresponding power obeys

    E_(K_t)(y)^r=E_K(y)^r
                    -t r E_K(y)^(r-1)C_E(y)+o(t),      (7)

again uniformly on U. In particular no centroid exception occurs.

For a finite actual family let its total mass be
M_t=M-t D+o(t), D=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z)v_z dS.
The normalized projective-aligned buffer has the uniform expansion

    f_hat_t(z,y)=(E_(K_z,t)(y)/M_t)^(1/N),
    dot f_hat_body(z,y)
       =(f_hat_0(z,y)/N)[-C_E,z(y)/E_z(y)+D/M].         (8)

This includes all signed source costs and the original-mass
normalization term; neither term is discarded.

## 4. A finite-contact minimum with moving bodies

Let J be a nonempty FINITE set of bases. At each z let ell_z(X) be a
fixed affine function, and suppose for the old buffer f_0 that

    psi_0(z,X)=ell_z(X)-epsilon f_0(z,X)>=0 on K_z,

with a UNIQUE zero y_z in int K_z. Let f_t be an energy power as in
(7), or its normalized version (8), and let A(t)=1+t a_1+o(t) be a
scalar. Define the attained minimum on the actual new bodies

    alpha(t)=min_(z in J, X in K_z,t)
                  [ell_z(X)-epsilon A(t)f_t(z,X)].     (9)

Then

    alpha(0)=0,
    alpha'(0+)=-epsilon max_(z in J)
                    [a_1 f_0(z,y_z)+dot f_body(z,y_z)]. (10)

No nesting or positivity of alpha is needed for (10).

First every minimizing point in (9) approaches the finite old contact
set. The old marks remain in the new bodies and give values O(t).
For any sequence of minimizers, compactness and Hausdorff convergence
give a subsequential limit in an old body. Joint continuity of the
energy at moving body/mark pairs makes its limit objective nonnegative
and at most zero, hence equal to zero at that base's unique y_z.
The required continuity includes boundary marks: E<=(d+1)T and the
hinge continuity argument give E->0 there. Thus no boundary or
remote minimizer has been silently omitted.

The localized marks now lie in compact interior neighborhoods, where
(7) or (8) is uniform. At a minimizing X_t in base z its expansion is

    psi_0(z,X_t)
       -epsilon t[a_1 f_0(z,X_t)+dot f_body(z,X_t)]+o(t).

The first term is nonnegative. Passing to a limiting contact proves
the lower derivative bound in (10); testing the finitely many old
marks proves the matching upper bound. This proves both existence
and the exact value of the right derivative.

For nested inward erosion, unnormalized f=E^(1/N), and A=1,
monotonicity gives alpha(t)>=0, and (10) becomes

    alpha'(0+)=(epsilon/N) min_(z in J)
                       E_z(y_z)^(-d/N) C_E,z(y_z).      (11)

In a translated equal-energy face the E_z are equal, but the physical
integrals C_E,z need not be equal; their MINIMUM must remain.

## 5. Application to the actual old buffered face

Use the buffered source and its fixed minimal deepest-base face F
from the preceding source, with f=E^(1/N). Let

    N_j=(a_j,u_j), ||u_j||=1,
    c_j=c_q(a_j,u_j),  mu(H_j)=q,
    rho_j>0, sum rho_j=1,
    h_0=sum rho_j c_j.

Put J=F intersect P. These are exactly the integer bases in that face
belonging to the old buffered deepest-base set: convexity of the
buffered region supplies a maximizing mark at every intermediate
integer base. Section 10's strict energy-power rigidity gives the
unique old contact mark y_z at each z in J. In particular the fixed
affine function

    ell_z(X)=sum_j rho_j N_j.(z,X)-h_0

satisfies every hypothesis of Section 4. Take A=1 and alpha(t) from
(9). For nested inward deformation its derivative is (11).

Assume the finitely selected caps have the following explicit regular
quantile data. Their old threshold derivatives are -S_j with S_j>0,
and near the old thresholds their actual perturbed tail masses satisfy

    mu_t{N_j.W>=c_j+s}
      =q-S_j s-t L_j+o(t+|s|).                        (12)

One sufficient geometric hypothesis for (12) is a continuous positive
threshold coarea at c_j and zero surface measure of each cut on every
old fiber boundary. The bounded radial shell expansion then gives
the uniform fixed-cap loss; threshold motion and continuity give
(12). More generally it is precisely (12) that is used. Unresolved
supporting-branch allocations are not included by declaration.

Let c_j(t,tau) denote the current proper local quantile of mass tau.
Its existence, uniqueness and local continuity follow from the positive
own section and the inner-homothet control. Equation (12) gives

    c_j(t,tau)=c_j-[(tau-q)+t L_j]/S_j+o(t+|tau-q|).

Choose the UNIQUE nearby common mass tau(t) by the EXACT equation

    sum_j rho_j c_j(t,tau(t))=h_0+alpha(t).             (13)

The left side is strictly decreasing in tau and its linear coefficient
at zero is -H, H=sum_j rho_j/S_j>0. The intermediate value theorem
and the preceding uniform expansion prove existence and uniqueness
near q, tau(t)=q+O(t), and

    tau'(0+)=-sum_j theta_j L_j-alpha'(0+)/H,
    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/H.                            (14)

This is an actual quantile equation, not a first-order assignment of
independent cap thresholds.

For every X in K_z,t at every z in J, the definition of alpha and
(13) give

    sum_j rho_j[N_j.(z,X)-c_j(t,tau(t))]
                    -epsilon f_t(z,X)>=0.

Hence at least one cap has buffered threshold at (z,X) no smaller
than its current tau(t)-quantile. Its actual buffered captured mass
is at most tau(t). Thus the whole ACTUAL MIXED PART of the old fixed
face is covered at this common
mass, rather than only a chosen moving source mark. Formula (11) is
therefore a valid additional face-level credit in (14).

## 6. Exact scope of global comparison

If finitely many such old faces cover all old buffered deepest bases,
apply (13) separately to each face. Under nested deformation,
mu_t<=mu_0 and f_t<=f_0 imply pointwise b_(epsilon,t)<=b_(epsilon,0)
on the new actual bodies. Every old nondeepest base has a strict gap
below q, uniformly because there are finitely many bases. For small t
these bases remain below all the continued masses q+O(t). Consequently

    Q_epsilon(t)<=max_i tau_i(t),
    upper Dini derivative Q_epsilon(t)
          <=max_i[-sum_j theta_ij L_ij-alpha_i'(0+)/H_i].

This needs no differentiable deepest path. For normalized depth the
original total-volume derivative contributes the usual q D/M term.
A strict decrease still requires an actual cost inequality for every
covering face; none is proved by the continuation theorem alone.

The normalized covariance buffer and nonnested global comparison are
being treated separately by slab_recovery_audit. Sections 1--4 supply
their uniform signed energy expansion and contact-minimum input,
including the scalar A(t) variation. They do not suppress changes of
the normal norm, total mass, or the finite old-contact set.

## 7. Exact homothetic calibration and its normalization warning

For d=1 let K_t=[-R_t,R_t], R_t=1-h t>0, with a fixed real h. Use
f_t=E^(1/2) and fixed epsilon with epsilon sqrt(2R_t)<R_t. The unique
buffered maximizing mark is zero, and exactly

    f_t(0)=sqrt(2R_t),
    Q_epsilon(t)=R_t+epsilon sqrt(2R_t).

For the two old caps with thresholds -epsilon sqrt(2), the fixed-cap
losses are L_1=L_2=h, coareas are one, and their equal weights give

    alpha(t)=epsilon sqrt(2)[1-sqrt(R_t)],
    alpha'(0)=epsilon h/sqrt(2),
    Q_epsilon'(0)=-h-epsilon h/sqrt(2).

These identities agree exactly with (10),(14), for either inward or
outward signs of h. Nevertheless the normalized derivative at fixed
epsilon is

    derivative [Q_epsilon(t)/(2R_t)] at zero
       =epsilon h/(2sqrt(2)).

For inward homothety it is positive, not negative. Thus even an exact
positive contact credit is NOT by itself a normalized descent proof;
the buffer's scale must be handled. In the covariance-normalized
variant, f_hat(0)=1 and Gamma_C(u)=|u|R_t/sqrt(3), so normalized
buffered depth is instead exactly 1/2+epsilon/(2sqrt(3)), independent
of R_t. This checks why both the norm and mass terms in that variant
must be retained.
